----Petitioner  Versus 1. State Of Rajasthan, Through Pp 2. Harlal S/o Chuna Ram, B/c- Nayak, R/o- 62 -Gb-A, P.s.

----Respondents For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Rajesh Saharan

For Respondent(s) : Mr. Vikram Sharma, PP  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE KULDEEP MATHUR Order 15/12/2023 This application for bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the petitioner who has been arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.166/2023 registered at Police Station Ramsinghpur, District Sri Ganganagar, for offences under Sections 363 and 366 of the IPC and Section 3/4(2) of the POCSO Act in alternate Section 376(3) of the IPC, under Section 5(L)/6 of POCSO Act in alternate Section 376(2)(N) of IPC under Section 5(J)(ii)/6 of POCSO Act and Section 3(2)(v) of SC/ST Act.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Public Prosecutor.
Perused the material available on record.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner who is aged about 22 years is behind the bars since [2023:RJ-JD:43960] (2 of 3) [CRLMB-12636/2023] 09.01.2023.

Learned counsel submitted that the prosecutrix in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. stated that she voluntarily eloped with the present petitioner and remained in his company out of her free will and volition for more than three months.

sentences.text: Learned counsel submitted that the allegations levelled by the prosecutrix in her court statement are false and the same do not inspire any confidence for the reason that in her court statements she has stated that she was travelling with the petitioner using public transportation and remained in his company, however, despite having ample opportunities she did not disclose the factum of her being abducted or subjected to sexual assault by the petitioner.

Learned counsel submitted that the petitioner is in judicial custody; statements of the prosecutrix have already been recorded before the competent criminal court and the trial of the case will take sufficiently long time, therefore, the benefit of bail may be granted to the accused-petitioner.
Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor has opposed the bail application.

Having considered the rival submissions, facts and circumstances of the case, this Court finds that the prosecutrix in her statements recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. stated that she voluntarily eloped with the present petitioner and remained in his company for more than three months.

This Court prima facie finds [2023:RJ-JD:43960] (3 of 3) [CRLMB-12636/2023] that the prosecutrix voluntarily eloped with the petitioner and remained in his company for more than three months,
travelled with him and also stayed with him in thickly populated areas.
The prosecutrix did not disclose the factum of she being abducted or subjected to sexual assault by the present petitioner despite having opportunities to do so.
Thus, without expressing any opinion on merits/demerits of the case, this Court is inclined to enlarge the petitioner on bail, who is aged about 22 years and is in judicial custody.
Consequently, the bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is allowed.

It is ordered that the accused-petitioner Akshay Kumar @ Sonu Singh S/o Shri Jagdish Kumar @ Manga Singh, arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.166/2023 registered at Police Station Ramsinghpur, District Sri Ganganagar, shall be released on bail, if not wanted in any other case, provided he furnishes a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- and two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each, to the satisfaction of learned trial court, for his appearance before that court on each & every date of hearing and whenever called upon to do so till completion of the trial.
(KULDEEP MATHUR),J 52-Hanuman/-
